newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin promises defence of shareholder rights.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin promises defence of shareholder rights.

text.p: Defence of shareholder rights is a top priority in reforming Russian companies this year, President Boris Yeltsin said.

Shareholder rights, a clear definition of the rights and duties of shareholders and managers, and perfecting corporate governance were all listed as key elements in enterprise reform in Yeltsin's annual written address to parliament, an advance copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Wednesday.
The document, which lays out measures to be taken by the government, also calls for contract law to be strengthened and for better management in companies partly or fully state owned.
Yeltsin also ordered the government to introduce by September 1 a programme for moving Russian companies to international accounting standards from 1998.

He noted that Russian accounting standards failed to provide managers, shareholders and investors with necessary information, and discussions about switching to international standards had been dragging on for five years.
